description: The main window's webview (label main) and nothing else, on the app's own pages only (local: true, no remote URLs). Keyed by webview label, not window label: Tauri grants a window-keyed capability to every webview inside the window, so a child webview later added to the main window gets none of this. App commands: the main-window permission (permissions/main-window.json), the commands the app shell's frontend calls. Plugins: only the calls the frontend makes. listen/unlisten for backend events and the drag-drop event; homeDir; the debug-build devtools shortcut. ask/open/save dialogs. Opening http(s)/mailto/tel links (opener:default); the same set lets the page reveal any path in the file manager, which the opener plugin cannot scope (it only shows the file, never opens or runs it). Writing files: the write permissions have no static scope, so a write succeeds only on paths a dialog added to the runtime fs scope: the file picked in a save dialog, a file picked in an open dialog, or the direct children of a folder picked in an open dialog (Add a folder to the Library, workspace sources, tool settings), until the app quits. Webview data folders stay denied (fs:deny-default). The webview reads no files through the fs plugin: documents are read through read_source_bytes and the other source commands, which serve indexed files only. Copy image of a snippet (clipboard write-image). The notification plugin's own page script asks whether notifications are allowed on macOS; notifications themselves are sent from Rust. Agent-built Artifacts previews never load here: they show in preview windows of their own label (preview-<id>), which no capability names, and the shodh-preview scheme refuses this webview (creations/preview.rs, preview_window.rs).
